name: Lockheed Martin Ventures
identity_check: Confirmed as Lockheed Martin Ventures (also 'LM Ventures', 'LMV'), the strategic corporate venture capital arm of Lockheed Martin Corporation (NYSE: LMT), founded 2007; its pages live at lockheedmartin.com/en-us/who-we-are/lockheed-martin-ventures.html, and lockheedmartinventures.com (cited in its press releases) redirects there. The fund's releases are datelined Bethesda, MD (parent HQ); a London office ('Lockheed Martin Ventures Europe') was announced 2026-07-16. Not the parent company's own acquisitions (e.g. the completed Terran Orbital acquisition listed on the LMV news page, or Ultra Maritime), not strategic investments announced by Lockheed Martin business areas without naming LMV (e.g. the Fortem $25M Series B tranche, announced by Lockheed Martin with the Rotary and Mission Systems president quoted; see conflicts), and not LM Evolve, a separate unit listed beside LM Ventures under 'Innovation & Investment' on lockheedmartin.com. Rounds were kept only where the source names Lockheed Martin Ventures, Lockheed Martin's venture arm, or 'Lockheed Martin' for a company on LMV's own portfolio page.

thesis_text.value: Corporate venture arm of Lockheed Martin backing deep-tech and dual-use startups whose technology complements or opens new parts of the national-security market: AI, autonomy, advanced manufacturing and materials, electronics, quantum, sensors/PNT, communications, propulsion and weapons. Invests from a $1B evergreen pool, offers engineering, facilities and supply-chain access, and grooms startups into Lockheed suppliers.

open_items: Check size: not stated on any LMV page or release; LMV's share of each round is undisclosed.

Stages: no stage policy stated. The 2022 fund-doubling page speaks of 'early-stage technology companies', the July 2026 release of 'investing earlier in the startup lifecycle', and the contact form accepts Pre-Seed through 'Series K+'; recorded rounds run from Series A to Series C plus a PIPE, so `stages` was left out.
Indian founders: nothing stated. The contact form's country list includes India (IN), which is not a policy statement.

requires_us_entity = 'no' is inferred from the July 2026 commitment to invest at least $100M in the UK and Europe (and non-US companies such as CloudNC, Satellite Vu and Q-CTRL on the portfolio page); no explicit entity policy is published.
HQ: Bethesda comes from a database address and the parent's Bethesda datelines; LMV's own pages give no office address. London office announced July 2026.

Fund history recorded as one evergreen fund ($1B, 2026-04-14). Earlier capacity steps: $100M (2007), $200M (2018, Global Venturing only), $400M (2022-08-02). The 'at least $100 million' UK/Europe earmark (2026-07-16) is a portion of the $1B and is not recorded as a separate fund.
No LMV-specific LinkedIn page is linked from the LMV site (only the Lockheed Martin corporate page); team bio pages carry no LinkedIn links.

Teradar (TechCrunch) and X-Bow (Defense Daily) name 'Lockheed Martin's venture arm'; recorded as Lockheed Martin Ventures. Havoc's release names 'Lockheed Martin' among existing investors; Havoc AI is on LMV's portfolio page.

Machina Labs: the user-supplied round list's 'Lockheed Martin' is confirmed as Lockheed Martin Ventures by the company release; no lead is named. A longer investor roster seen in database snippets (e.g. NVIDIA nVentures) was not verified.
REGENT's $240M is an equal mix of equity and debt; Erebor Bank provided the debt. Elroy Air's $175M is total PIPE commitments ($75M funded) ahead of its SPAC merger, recorded as stage 'strategic'.

The web-search budget ran out partway through, so these database-hinted LMV rounds could not be confirmed on a round page: Firestorm Labs $47M Series A (2025), Nooks Series A (2025), X-Bow $105M Series B (2025), South 8 Technologies $11M (Dec 2025), Radiant Series D (mentioned by Global Venturing), Inversion Space $44M (Nov 2024; BusinessWire page blocked), and new 2026 portfolio companies Diffraqtion and Living Optics. Senra Systems' Series A and B releases do not name LMV.

Founding year not found for most round companies; HQ country not stated on the fetched round pages for Agile Space Industries, Venus Aerospace and X-Bow Systems. X-Bow interim round dated by the Defense Daily article (2023-11-17); amount undisclosed.

Team members without a stated industrial/AI/hardware focus or bio (John Richmond, Katie Swanson, Rathik Patel, Kaija Gisolfi-McCready and the analysts) are not recorded as partners. A database lists older staff (Ali Perez, Xiaoming Yin, Elizabeth Onasanya) who are not on the current team page.
